description: Dark stone terraced in bands, a seam of live gold running the length of them. It lights whatever pouch you put it in.
lore: It is the only one a smith will not work after dark, and the reason is practical rather than nervous. The seam in it is live. Put it on the bench beside heated metal and there is no telling the colour of the work from the colour coming off the stone, so the setting gets done at noon with the doors open, by people who otherwise keep their doors shut in order to read the heat. Dark stone, terraced in bands the whole way up, gold running the length of the banding and brightest across the middle, one red fleck low on it that is neither. It does not go down when you put it away.

This is the piece that costs something to hold. Wrapped twice in hide it still finds the seams of a pouch, and you do not carry one and also arrive anywhere unannounced. Handlers on the eastern ground say the two best stones that country gives up are exact opposites, and that a sensible person carries one and not both. Set to an edge it burns what the edge touches. Set close, it does the other thing, and the smiths are careful to say they only sell it and have never once needed it.

The size of it starts to bother you after a while. Every hard piece lends a little of what it remembers: a stone off something that burned will warm the room it is in and no more, though the creature it came off could have taken a wood with it. This one lends nothing little. It does the entire thing, undiminished, out of a lump you can close a hand round. The inference is short and unwelcome. The light was never spread through that animal at all. It was already this small, in there, with a body built round it, and what came across the black wood on its hands was the carrying-case.

The bands are the part that gets counted. Layers are read the way layers are read anywhere, as one habit laid over another over a long time doing the same thing, and a banded piece is taken as evidence of an age of it. Count the bands on this one and you get a number. Then set the number beside what it came off: a shape that went into the ground one way and came out the other with its light already burning, and no age behind it worth the name. Either the layers mean nothing here, in which case the reading is worth nothing anywhere, or they are an honest record of a very long time and that time was not the creature's. The counting gets done anyway. It is done quietly, with the bag already tied.
